subject: Hosted API: Geofence retention execution plan & erasure SLA
messages:
From: Talia Ramos <security@prospectcorp.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@prospectcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API: residency, retention and erasure questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. Our security team asked for a short follow-up on three items to include in our vendor risk assessment:

1) How is geofencing enforced for the hosted API? If we select EU-only residency, can you confirm that inference logs, cached KV state, and stored artifacts are pinned to EU regions only?

2) What are your default retention windows for: request logs, request/response payloads, embeddings, and audit logs? Please split by 'default' and 'customer-configurable' where applicable.

3) Deletion workflow: if ProspectCorp requests a full purge of tenant data, what steps does Redwood take, how long until data is irrecoverable (including backups/snapshots), and what evidence can you provide?

We appreciate concise answers we can include in our questionnaire.

Best,
Talia
Talia Ramos
Security Analyst, ProspectCorp
[ProspectCorp headquarters]
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Talia Ramos <security@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API: residency, retention and erasure questions

Hi Talia —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can paste into your questionnaire; I also attached a short PDF (redwood_retention_overview.pdf) and our SOC 2 summary. I copied Ben (sales legal) and Rishi (support) for SLA/operation details.

1) Geofencing/enforcement
- Customers choose region at provisioning; for hosted API we pin model storage and customer tenant artifacts to the selected region cluster (EU in your case).
- Processing: inference compute may touch ephemeral worker nodes that are co-located in the selected region. Control-plane metadata (orchestration tasks) may operate from control endpoints; however no customer payload is stored outside the selected region cluster.
- KV cache and short-lived prefix caches: by default these are in-memory on node pools in the chosen region. They are not replicated to other regions unless cross-region routing is explicitly configured.

2) Retention windows (defaults + configurable)
- Request logs (metadata only: timestamps, routing, token usage): default 30 days; configurable down to 0 via enterprise retention policy.
- Request/response payloads (full text/embeddings): default 30 days for hosted API (used for safety/abuse detection and quality monitoring); customers on Dedicated/Private can opt for 0-day retention in the tenancy config. We offer an addendum for hosted customers to reduce retention and enable stricter controls under a DPA.
- Generated embeddings stored by customer-specific index services: default 90 days if retained by Redwood-managed indices; customers can export or request immediate deletion.
- Audit logs (access, admin actions): retained 365 days by default for auditability; retention can be shortened for enterprise plans upon request.

3) Deletion workflow and evidence
- Initiation: customer can open a support ticket or use the Console 'Tenant Erase' action (we can perform on your behalf).
- Immediate actions: we mark the tenant data as 'soft-deleted' and revoke access tokens; observable acknowledgement issued within 24 hours.
- Purge schedule: primary storage objects are purged on background jobs; expected irrecoverability for primary stores within 30 days of request.
- Backups & snapshots: periodic backups are retained for disaster recovery and have a 90-day TTL by default; we schedule targeted snapshot expiration and deletion during purge — final irrecoverability across backups can be up to 90 days unless an emergency purge is negotiated.
- Evidence: after purge we can provide a signed deletion attestation and references to storage object IDs removed. For SOC 2 customers we can provide audit artifacts under NDA.

Additional operational notes
- KV/in-memory caches: ephemeral and not written to long-term blob storage; lifespan is measured in hours (typical TTL 0–2 hours) unless configured for longer caching for performance.
- Prefix caching: tombstoned on tenant erase and not included in backups.
- Embeddings & retrievers: if stored in Redwood-managed indices we run index compaction and delete entries; we provide a manifest of deleted index IDs.

If you want, Ben can put together a short DPA amendment (three bullets) to reduce hosted default retention and shorten backup TTLs for ProspectCorp. I attached the overview PDF and SOC 2 summary.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Talia Ramos <security@prospectcorp.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@prospectcorp.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API: residency, retention and erasure questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks, this is very helpful. Two quick clarifications before we loop legal:

- Backups: you note a 90-day TTL by default. Can you confirm whether backups are geo-redundant (i.e., replicated to a second region) and whether those replicas are also subject to the same region-locking constraints? ProspectCorp requires that secondary replicas for EU tenants remain in EU.

- Evidence/manifest: is the deletion manifest generated automatically as part of the job, or is it produced on-request by Support? We prefer an automated manifest to feed into our compliance pipeline.

If you can confirm those two points we can move to legal/DPA review.

Best,
Talia
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Talia Ramos <security@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 15:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API: residency, retention and erasure questions

Hi Talia — quick answers to those two bullets, and looping Ben for the DPA/amendment next steps.

- Backups/replication: for EU tenants, backup replicas are confined to EU regions by default. We do not replicate EU tenant backups to non-EU regions unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region DR. Replication topology is documented in the attached PDF.

- Deletion manifest: we can produce an automated manifest as part of the purge job. For Enterprise/DPA customers we emit a machine-readable manifest (JSON/CSV) with object IDs, deletion timestamps, and job run IDs. We can push the manifest to a secure S3 location or to your SIEM via a signed transfer.

Ben — can you share a short DPA amendment draft and the DocuSign link? Rishi — help please on a short note describing emergency purge SLA (we currently target <72 hours for emergency purge execution once legal signs an amendment).

Thanks — attaching a draft DPA amendment and DocuSign placeholder for your legal team.

Best,
Kim
